title: Community Foundation of Southeastern Alberta Award
audience: Graduating High School Seniors in Medicine Hat
notes: Contact your school guidance counsellor to apply.
description: The Community Foundation of Southeastern Alberta Award provides $1,000 to graduating high school seniors in Medicine Hat who demonstrate community involvement and academic achievement. This award recognizes students who have made meaningful contributions to their local community. Applicants should contact their school guidance counselor to apply.

title: Medicine Hat College Entrance Scholarship
audience: First-year MHC students
description: This scholarship is awarded by Medicine Hat College to support first-year students entering the college. The $2,500 award recognizes academic achievement and helps students succeed in their post-secondary studies.

title: Kinsmen Club of Medicine Hat Grant
audience: Students demonstrating community service
description: The Kinsmen Club of Medicine Hat offers a $500 grant to high school students who demonstrate a strong commitment to community service and volunteerism. This award recognizes students who make a positive impact in their local community through active participation in service initiatives.

title: South Country Co-op Scholarship
audience: High school students in the South Country Co-op trading area
notes: Family must be a South Country Co-op member with minimum $2,000 in purchases. Apply by mail or email to j.doll@sccoop.ca.
description: South Country Co-op offers a $1,000 scholarship to high school students whose families are members of South Country Co-op with at least $2,000 in purchases. This award recognizes student achievement within the Co-op's trading area in the Medicine Hat region. Applicants should contact j.doll@sccoop.ca or apply by mail for more information.

title: Alberta Indigenous Careers Award
audience: Indigenous Albertans pursuing in-demand careers
description: This $4,000 award supports Indigenous Albertans who are pursuing careers in high-demand sectors. Eligible applicants must be Indigenous (First Nations, Métis, or Inuit) high school graduates or current high school students preparing to enter post-secondary education in Alberta.

title: RE/MAX Quest for Excellence
audience: Graduating high school students demonstrating leadership
description: RE/MAX Quest for Excellence is a $1,000 scholarship awarded by RE/MAX to graduating high school students in the Medicine Hat region who demonstrate strong leadership qualities. This award recognizes students who show promise in their community and are preparing to enter post-secondary education.

title: MHPSD Financial Assistance
audience: MHPSD students needing financial assistance
description: The Medicine Hat Public School District (MHPSD) offers this $500 financial assistance award to support graduating high school students demonstrating financial need. This scholarship helps eligible MHPSD students transition to post-secondary education by providing direct financial support.

title: Alexander Rutherford Scholarship
audience: Alberta high school students based on academic averages
description: The Alexander Rutherford Scholarship is offered to Alberta high school students who demonstrate strong academic achievement. This $2,500 award recognizes graduating seniors based on their academic averages and supports their transition to post-secondary education.

title: Cypress County Agricultural Scholarship
audience: Students from Cypress County pursuing ag-related studies
description: This $1,000 scholarship supports high school students from Cypress County who are pursuing agriculture-related studies. It recognizes students committed to advancing their skills in the agricultural trades sector. Applicants should demonstrate interest in agriculture and be eligible to enter post-secondary agricultural programs.

title: Medicine Hat Exhibition & Stampede Scholarship
audience: Local students pursuing agriculture, trades, or western heritage
notes: Contact your school guidance counsellor to apply.
description: The Medicine Hat Exhibition & Stampede provides this $1,000 scholarship to support local high school students pursuing careers in agriculture, trades, or who have a passion for western heritage. This award recognizes students committed to these fields and is open to graduates entering post-secondary education. Interested applicants should contact their school guidance counsellor to learn more about applying.

title: Servus Credit Union Young Adult Scholarship
audience: Servus Credit Union members entering post-secondary
notes: Contact your school guidance counsellor to apply.
description: Servus Credit Union offers this $1,500 scholarship to support members who are entering post-secondary education. Applicants must be Servus Credit Union members in good standing. Contact your school guidance counsellor for application details.

title: ATB Financial Indigenous Education Award
audience: Indigenous students studying business or finance in Alberta
description: ATB Financial awards $1,500 annually to Indigenous students pursuing business or finance studies in Alberta. This award recognizes and supports Indigenous learners as they advance their education in these fields. Applicants must be Indigenous and enrolled or planning to enroll in post-secondary business or finance programs.

title: ATA Local 21 Scholarship
audience: Children of Elk Island Catholic Schools teachers (Sherwood Park, Fort Saskatchewan, Camrose, Vegreville area)
notes: Contact ATA Local 21 at atalocal21@gmail.com to apply. For children of Elk Island Catholic Schools educators only.
description: The ATA Local 21 Scholarship, offered by the Alberta Teachers' Association Local 21, provides $1,000 to recognize academic achievement. This scholarship is exclusively for children of educators employed by Elk Island Catholic Schools in the Sherwood Park, Fort Saskatchewan, Camrose, and Vegreville areas.

title: Medicine Hat Police Association Bursary
audience: Local high school graduates pursuing criminal justice
notes: Contact your school guidance counsellor to apply.
description: The Medicine Hat Police Association awards this $500 bursary to support local high school graduates pursuing criminal justice studies. Open to graduating seniors in Medicine Hat who demonstrate financial need and plan to continue their education in criminal justice programs.

title: Medicine Hat Women in Business Bursary
audience: Female students entering business programs
notes: Contact your school guidance counsellor to apply.
description: This $500 bursary supports female high school graduates from the Medicine Hat area who are entering business programs at post-secondary institutions. Applicants should demonstrate financial need and contact their school's guidance counsellor to apply.

title: Hat High (MHHS) Alumni Memorial Scholarship
audience: Graduating students from Medicine Hat High School
notes: Contact your school guidance counsellor to apply.
description: This $1,000 award is offered by Hat High School alumni to recognize graduating students from Medicine Hat High School. The scholarship celebrates academic achievement and supports students as they transition to post-secondary education. Interested applicants should contact their school guidance counsellor for application details.

title: Crescent Heights High School Leadership Award
audience: Graduating students from CHHS demonstrating leadership
notes: Contact your school guidance counsellor to apply.
description: Crescent Heights High School awards this $500 leadership award to graduating students who have demonstrated exceptional leadership skills and community involvement. Applicants should contact their school guidance counsellor to learn more about eligibility and how to apply.

title: Monsignor McCoy Faith in Action Award
audience: Graduating students from McCoy Catholic High School
notes: Contact your school guidance counsellor to apply.
description: Monsignor McCoy Catholic High School offers the Faith in Action Award to recognize graduating students who exemplify community service and faith-based values. This $500 award celebrates students who demonstrate a commitment to serving their community and living out their faith. Students should contact their school guidance counsellor to apply.

title: Saamis Memorial Funeral Chapel Scholarship
audience: Local students pursuing healthcare or mortuary science
notes: Contact your school guidance counsellor to apply.
description: Saamis Memorial Funeral Chapel offers this $1,000 scholarship to local Medicine Hat high school students pursuing healthcare or mortuary science at the post-secondary level. This award recognizes academic achievement and commitment to caring professions. Apply through your school's guidance counsellor.

title: Medicine Hat Rotary Club Music Festival Award
audience: Participants in the local Rotary Music Festival
notes: Contact your school guidance counsellor to apply.
description: The Medicine Hat Rotary Club offers this $500 award to recognize musical talent and achievement among participants in the local Rotary Music Festival. This award celebrates students' dedication to the arts and supports their continued musical pursuits.

title: Medicine Hat Lions Club Community Grant
audience: Students with strong volunteer history in Medicine Hat
description: The Medicine Hat Lions Club awards this $1,000 community grant to recognize students who have demonstrated a strong commitment to volunteer work in the Medicine Hat area. This award celebrates local youth who give back to their community through service and engagement.

title: Tradesecrets Alberta Apprenticeship Scholarship
audience: Alberta registered apprentices
description: This $1,000 scholarship supports Alberta registered apprentices pursuing trades careers. Offered to recognize and assist students committed to apprenticeship training programs in the province. Eligible applicants must be enrolled in a recognized Alberta apprenticeship program.

title: Southeastern Alberta Regional Science Fair Award
audience: Top senior projects at the SEAR Science Fair
description: This $500 award recognizes top student projects at the Southeastern Alberta Regional (SEAR) Science Fair in Medicine Hat. It supports high school students pursuing excellence in STEM fields and showcasing innovative scientific research.

title: City of Medicine Hat Environmental Bursary
audience: Students pursuing environmental sciences
notes: Contact your school guidance counsellor to apply.
description: The City of Medicine Hat offers this $1,000 bursary to support high school students in the Medicine Hat region who are pursuing environmental sciences. This need-based award is for graduating seniors entering post-secondary studies or current high school students with a demonstrated commitment to environmental studies.

title: Belcourt Brosseau Métis Awards
audience: Métis students in Alberta pursuing post-secondary education
description: The Belcourt Brosseau Métis Awards provide $10,000 to support Métis students in Alberta as they pursue post-secondary education. These awards recognize and celebrate Métis learners transitioning from high school to higher education across the province.

title: Kermet Archibald & Jacoba Van den Brink Memorial Scholarship
audience: Graduating Calgary CBE/CCSD high school students entering science, health, engineering, or trades
description: This $25,000 memorial scholarship honours Kermet Archibald and Jacoba Van den Brink by supporting graduating high school students from Calgary's CBE and CCSD boards who are pursuing studies in science, health, engineering, or trades. Applicants must be entering a post-secondary institution and demonstrate commitment to these fields of study.

title: Marguerite Patricia P. Bannister Memorial Degree Awards
audience: Graduating Calgary CBE/CCSD high school students entering University of Calgary
description: This $4,000 award honors the legacy of Marguerite Patricia P. Bannister by supporting graduating high school students from Calgary's CBE and CCSD schools who are entering the University of Calgary. The scholarship recognizes academic achievement and assists students as they transition to university-level studies.

title: Bill Gibson Bursary
audience: Graduating Calgary-area high school student entering post-secondary
description: The Bill Gibson Bursary is a $10,000 award for graduating high school students from the Calgary area who are entering post-secondary studies. This bursary recognizes and supports students as they transition from secondary to post-secondary education.

title: Optimist Club William J. Cummer Scholarship
audience: Graduating Calgary high school students with community involvement
description: The Optimist Club William J. Cummer Scholarship awards $2,500 to graduating Calgary high school students who demonstrate strong community involvement. This award recognizes the value of youth engagement in their local community and is offered by the Optimist Club to support students as they transition to post-secondary education.

title: Calgary Flames Foundation Community Involvement Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 Calgary CBE/CCSD students demonstrating leadership through volunteering
description: The Calgary Flames Foundation awards $2,000 to Grade 12 students from Calgary CBE and CCSD schools who demonstrate strong leadership through community volunteering. This scholarship recognizes students committed to making a positive impact in their community.

title: Edith Berger Memorial Scholarship
audience: Graduating Calgary CBE/CCSD students planning to study Education/Teaching
description: The Edith Berger Memorial Scholarship recognizes graduating Calgary high school students who are pursuing studies in Education or Teaching. This $1,000 award supports students from Calgary Board of Education and Calgary Catholic School District who are committed to entering the teaching profession.

title: Big Brothers Big Sisters Society of Calgary Scholarship
audience: Graduating Calgary CBE/CCSD students
description: Big Brothers Big Sisters Society of Calgary offers this $1,000 scholarship to graduating high school students who demonstrate involvement in their community. This award recognizes students from Calgary's CBE and CCSD who exemplify the values of mentorship and civic engagement.

title: Eimer Scholarship Fund Award for Health Care
audience: Graduating Calgary CBE/CCSD students entering health care programs
description: The Eimer Scholarship Fund Award for Health Care supports graduating high school students in Calgary who are pursuing post-secondary education in health care fields. This $2,000 award recognizes students' commitment to careers in health and is available to eligible students from Calgary Board of Education and Calgary Catholic School District schools.

title: Alex Tutschek FCPA Award for Indigenous Student Achievement
audience: Grade 12 Indigenous Alberta students entering a business program
description: The Alex Tutschek FCPA Award recognizes Indigenous students from Alberta who demonstrate excellence and are pursuing business education at the post-secondary level. This $1,500 award celebrates Indigenous student achievement in business and supports their academic journey.

title: CPA Alberta Young Emerging Professional Award
audience: Grade 12 Alberta students demonstrating professionalism, integrity, and leadership
description: CPA Alberta presents this $1,500 award to Grade 12 students across Alberta who demonstrate exceptional professionalism, integrity, and leadership. The award recognizes students who embody values important to the accounting profession and are preparing to enter post-secondary education.

title: David Bentley FCPA and Janet Bentley High School Excellence Award
audience: Grade 12 Alberta students, preference for those relocating within AB for post-secondary
description: The David Bentley FCPA and Janet Bentley High School Excellence Award recognizes academic achievement among graduating Grade 12 students in Alberta. This $2,500 award is presented to students who demonstrate excellence in their studies, with preference given to those planning to pursue post-secondary education within Alberta.

title: CPA Alberta Empowered Young Woman Award
audience: Grade 12 Alberta students who identify as a girl/woman
description: CPA Alberta offers this $2,000 award to recognize and empower young women pursuing post-secondary education. The award is available to Grade 12 students in Alberta who identify as girls or women and demonstrate academic excellence. This award celebrates the achievements of female students as they transition to post-secondary studies.

title: Kelly & Creaghan Stepping Up in the Community Award
audience: Grade 12 Alberta students who demonstrate leadership through volunteering
description: This $2,000 award recognizes Grade 12 Alberta students who demonstrate exceptional leadership and commitment to their communities through volunteer service. The Kelly & Creaghan Stepping Up in the Community Award celebrates young people making a positive difference through civic engagement and helping others.

title: Michael Burnyeat FCPA Sparking Great Careers High School Award
audience: Grade 12 Alberta students entering BBA, B.Mgmt, or B.Comm at an Alberta institution
description: The Michael Burnyeat FCPA Sparking Great Careers High School Award is offered to Grade 12 Alberta high school students entering business-focused post-secondary programs. This $1,250 award recognizes students pursuing Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA), Bachelor of Management (B.Mgmt), or Bachelor of Commerce (B.Comm) degrees at Alberta institutions. The award aims to spark great careers for aspiring business professionals.

title: Paula Weiss & Spencer Weiss BIPOC Success Award
audience: Grade 12 Alberta BIPOC students demonstrating good character and leadership
description: The Paula Weiss & Spencer Weiss BIPOC Success Award recognizes Grade 12 students from Black, Indigenous, and People of Color backgrounds across Alberta who demonstrate strong character and leadership qualities. This $2,500 award supports BIPOC students as they transition to post-secondary education or other pursuits.

title: Horatio Alger Association of Canada Scholarship
audience: Alberta students with financial need (under $65,000 family income), 65% minimum average
description: The Horatio Alger Association of Canada provides scholarships to recognize students who overcome adversity and demonstrate outstanding character. Alberta high school graduating seniors with demonstrated financial need (family income under $65,000) and a minimum 65% average are eligible to apply. This award supports Canadian students entering post-secondary education.

title: WorldSkills Provincial Champion Scholarship
audience: Top 2 Grade 12 podium finishers at the Provincial Skills Canada Competition
notes: Awarded to Alberta students who win a WorldSkills provincial championship. Apply through your school or Alberta Student Aid. Amount is $1,200.
description: This $1,200 scholarship recognizes Alberta Grade 12 students who achieve top finishes at the Provincial Skills Canada Competition in their respective trade fields. Applicants must be among the top 2 podium finishers at the provincial level to be eligible. Students can apply through their school or Alberta Student Aid.

title: First Nations, Métis and Inuit Bursary
audience: Indigenous students pursuing post-secondary education, return-of-service in northern Alberta
description: This $11,500 bursary supports First Nations, Métis, and Inuit students pursuing post-secondary education in Alberta. Recipients are expected to provide return-of-service in northern Alberta communities. The award recognizes Indigenous students' educational aspirations and commitment to their regions.

title: New Beginnings Bursary
audience: Alberta students eligible for full-time student loan funding entering post-secondary
description: The New Beginnings Bursary supports Alberta high school graduates as they transition to post-secondary education. This $5,000 bursary is available to students who are eligible for full-time student loan funding. It recognizes the financial needs of students beginning their post-secondary journey.

title: Loran Scholarship
audience: Canadian high school students — each school may nominate up to 3 students
description: The Loran Scholarship is a prestigious national award recognizing academic excellence, offering $100,000 to outstanding Canadian high school students. Each school may nominate up to 3 graduating students entering post-secondary education. This award celebrates leadership and achievement among Canada's top high school performers.

title: Schulich Leader Scholarships
audience: Canadian high school students entering STEM at one of 20 selected universities — school nominates 1 student
description: The Schulich Leader Scholarships recognize exceptional Canadian high school students pursuing STEM at one of 20 select Canadian universities. Recipients are nominated by their school and receive $100,000 to support their post-secondary education. Eligible students must be graduating high school seniors planning to enter a STEM program at a participating institution.

title: TD Scholarships for Community Leadership
audience: Canadian students with 75%+ GPA and significant community involvement
description: TD Scholarships for Community Leadership is offered by TD Bank to recognize Canadian high school students who demonstrate exceptional academic achievement and significant involvement in their communities. This $70,000 scholarship supports graduating seniors with a 75% or higher GPA who have made meaningful contributions through community service and leadership activities.

title: Terry Fox Humanitarian Award
audience: Canadian students demonstrating humanitarian work, up to 4 years of funding
description: The Terry Fox Humanitarian Award recognizes Canadian high school students who demonstrate exceptional commitment to humanitarian work and community service. This prestigious award provides up to $28,000 in funding over four years to support recipients' post-secondary education. Students are selected based on their humanitarian contributions and dedication to making a positive impact in their communities.

title: Advancing Futures Bursary
audience: Alberta youth aged 18–24 who have been in government care (foster care) at any point
description: The Advancing Futures Bursary provides up to $40,000 in financial support to Alberta youth aged 18–24 who have experienced government care (foster care). This award recognizes the challenges faced by young people who have been in the care system and aims to help them pursue post-secondary education and achieve their goals.

title: UCalgary Pathways to Medicine Scholarship
audience: High school students applying to University of Calgary undergraduate programs
notes: For low-income, rural, and Indigenous applicants to UCalgary undergraduate programs. Award is $5,000/year renewable for up to 4 years (up to $20,000 total). Apply through UCalgary Awards Hub.
description: The University of Calgary offers this renewable scholarship of up to $5,000 per year (up to $20,000 total over four years) to support low-income, rural, and Indigenous high school students entering UCalgary's undergraduate programs. This award recognizes the potential of students from underrepresented backgrounds pursuing STEM fields and helps make post-secondary education more accessible.

title: Keyera Energy — Peter J. Renton Memorial Scholarship
audience: Alberta residents entering first year of an oil & gas related degree or diploma at an AB institution
description: Keyera Energy offers this $6,000 scholarship to Alberta residents pursuing an oil and gas-related degree or diploma at an Alberta post-secondary institution. Named after Peter J. Renton, this award recognizes students entering their first year of study in STEM fields related to the energy sector. Applicants must be graduating high school seniors planning to attend an Alberta institution.

title: NADC Northern Alberta Development Council Bursary
audience: Alberta residents planning to enroll full-time in post-secondary, with return-of-service in northern AB
description: The Northern Alberta Development Council offers this $12,000 bursary to Alberta residents who are planning to enroll full-time in post-secondary education. Recipients are expected to commit to a return-of-service requirement in northern Alberta after completing their studies.

title: MindFuel Science Scholarships
audience: Alberta high school graduates entering first year of science or science education at an AB institution
description: MindFuel Science Scholarships support Alberta high school graduates who are pursuing first-year studies in science or science education at an Alberta post-secondary institution. This $5,000 award recognizes students committed to advancing scientific knowledge and education in the province.

title: Premier's Citizenship Award
audience: Alberta high school students — each school nominates ONE student per year
description: The Premier's Citizenship Award recognizes Alberta high school students who demonstrate exceptional commitment to their communities. Each school nominates one graduating student annually to receive this $7,005 award in recognition of their citizenship and community contributions.

title: Calgary Stampede Grade 12 Western Art Scholarship
audience: Southern Alberta Grade 12 students who create western art
description: The Calgary Stampede awards this $2,000 scholarship to Grade 12 students in Southern Alberta who demonstrate excellence in western art. This award celebrates artistic talent inspired by the traditions and culture of the Canadian West, supporting students as they prepare for post-secondary education.

title: ASAA Alberta Milk Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 ASAA member school students — school nominates 1 male + 1 female student
description: The ASAA Alberta Milk Scholarship recognizes academic achievement among high school students in Alberta. One male and one female student from ASAA member schools are nominated and awarded $1,000 each by their schools.

title: Anna & John Kolesar Memorial Scholarship
audience: Alberta residents pursuing an Education degree, first-generation university student
description: The Anna & John Kolesar Memorial Scholarship supports Alberta high school graduates who are first-generation university students pursuing an Education degree. This $1,500 award recognizes students committed to becoming educators and opening doors for their families through higher education.

title: IODE Coronation Bursary
audience: Alberta high school students entering any degree program in AB, 3+ years AB resident, financial need
description: The IODE (Imperial Order Daughters of the Empire) Coronation Bursary supports Alberta high school students who demonstrate financial need and plan to pursue any degree program at an Alberta post-secondary institution. Applicants must have been Alberta residents for at least three years. This $1,000 bursary helps make higher education more accessible for deserving students.

title: RAP/CTS Apprenticeship Scholarships
audience: Alberta high school students in the Registered Apprenticeship Program or CTS apprenticeship pathway
description: This $1,000 scholarship supports Alberta high school students pursuing a career in the trades through enrollment in the Registered Apprenticeship Program (RAP) or CTS apprenticeship pathway. The award recognizes students committed to developing skilled trades expertise and preparing for a rewarding apprenticeship career.

title: Canadian Natural Resources Scholarship
audience: Students entering technical or trades training related to oil & gas at accredited institutions
description: Canadian Natural Resources offers a $3,000 scholarship to support students pursuing technical or trades training in the oil and gas sector at accredited Alberta institutions. This award recognizes students committed to careers in this essential industry and helps offset the costs of specialized training programs.

title: Bayer Fund Opportunity Scholarship
audience: Canadian final-year high school students entering agriculture, food science, or culinary programs
description: The Bayer Fund offers this scholarship to Canadian high school graduates pursuing agriculture, food science, or culinary programs at post-secondary institutions. This $1,500 award recognizes students entering these fields and supports their transition to higher education in these important industries.

title: Dr. Ernest and Minnie Mehl Scholarship
audience: Alberta students — automatically considered when applying for the Alexander Rutherford Scholarship
description: The Dr. Ernest and Minnie Mehl Scholarship is an Alberta-based academic award of $3,500 for high school students preparing to enter post-secondary education. Students are automatically considered for this scholarship when applying for the Alexander Rutherford Scholarship, making it part of Alberta's broader support for academic achievement.

title: Catherine and Robert Povaschuk Scholarship
audience: Edmonton Public Schools Grade 12 students with honours standing, conditional acceptance to UofA
description: This $1,500 scholarship is awarded to Grade 12 students from Edmonton Public Schools who demonstrate honours standing and have received conditional acceptance to the University of Alberta. The Catherine and Robert Povaschuk Scholarship recognizes academic excellence and supports students as they transition to post-secondary education.

title: Betty Finch Scholarship
audience: Edmonton Public Schools Grade 12 students
description: The Betty Finch Scholarship is awarded to academically accomplished graduating students in Edmonton Public Schools. This $1,000 scholarship recognizes excellence and supports Grade 12 students as they pursue post-secondary education.

title: Esther and Peter Cunliffe Scholarship
audience: Edmonton Public Schools Grade 12 students
description: The Esther and Peter Cunliffe Scholarship awards $1,000 to graduating Grade 12 students in Edmonton Public Schools who demonstrate academic excellence. This award supports students as they transition to post-secondary education.

title: Grace Elaine Campbell Scholarship
audience: Edmonton Public Schools Grade 12 students
description: The Grace Elaine Campbell Scholarship recognizes academic achievement among graduating high school students in Edmonton. This $1,000 award is available to Grade 12 students enrolled in Edmonton Public Schools who demonstrate excellence in their studies.

title: James P. Jones Scholarship
audience: Edmonton Public Schools Grade 12 students
description: The James P. Jones Scholarship awards $1,000 to outstanding Grade 12 students in Edmonton Public Schools. This academic award recognizes achievement and is available to graduating seniors preparing to enter post-secondary education.

title: Sandra B. Woitas Opportunity Through Education Scholarship
audience: Edmonton Public Schools Grade 12 students demonstrating educational commitment
description: This $1,000 scholarship, offered through the Edmonton Public Schools community, recognizes Grade 12 students who demonstrate strong educational commitment. It aims to support graduating students as they transition to post-secondary education.

title: LeRoy Warden & Associates Scholarship
audience: Edmonton Public Schools Grade 12 students
description: LeRoy Warden & Associates offers this $1,000 scholarship to graduating Grade 12 students in Edmonton Public Schools. This award recognizes academic achievement and supports students as they transition to post-secondary education.

title: Winspear Fund Scholarships for Classical Music
audience: Students in Edmonton or Northern Alberta pursuing advanced classical music study
description: The Winspear Fund provides scholarships to support students from Edmonton and Northern Alberta who are pursuing advanced study in classical music. These awards are designed to help talented musicians continue their arts education at a post-secondary level. Applicants should demonstrate serious commitment to classical music study.

title: Ranald and Vera Shean Memorial Scholarships
audience: Students age 12+ in Edmonton or Northern Alberta pursuing violin or piano study
description: The Ranald and Vera Shean Memorial Scholarships support students aged 12 and older in Edmonton and Northern Alberta who are pursuing violin or piano study. These $8,000 awards recognize dedication to musical excellence in classical string and keyboard instruments. Applicants should demonstrate commitment to their musical development and a passion for performance.

title: Mah Society of Edmonton Centennial Scholarship
audience: Students with the surname "Mah" entering post-secondary in Canada
notes: Open to students with the surname "Mah" of any background. Offered by the Mah Society of Edmonton. Contact the Society directly for application details.
description: The Mah Society of Edmonton offers this $1,000 centennial scholarship to students entering post-secondary education in Canada who carry the surname "Mah." This award celebrates the contributions of the Mah community and is open to students of any background and academic achievement level.

title: Don and Norine Lowry Awards for Women of Excellence
audience: Women in Edmonton pursuing post-secondary studies in energy, power, water, business, finance, or safety
description: The Don and Norine Lowry Awards for Women of Excellence support women in the Edmonton area who are pursuing post-secondary education in energy, power, water, business, finance, or safety. This $5,000 award recognizes outstanding female students committed to careers in these critical industries. Eligible applicants must be graduating high school seniors preparing to enter post-secondary studies.

title: Lethbridge School Division ICE Scholarship
audience: Lethbridge School Division students demonstrating innovation, creativity, and entrepreneurship
description: The Lethbridge School Division offers this $1,000 scholarship to recognize and support students who demonstrate innovation, creativity, and entrepreneurial thinking. This award celebrates students who show initiative and original problem-solving within their school community. Eligible applicants must be students attending schools within the Lethbridge School Division.

title: Lethbridge County Community Benefit Scholarship
audience: High school students in Lethbridge County area entering STEM programs
description: The Lethbridge County Community Benefit Scholarship supports high school students in the Lethbridge County area who are pursuing post-secondary studies in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) fields. This $2,000 award recognizes academic achievement and commitment to science and technology education. Students must be graduating from a Lethbridge County high school and planning to enter a STEM program at a post-secondary institution.

title: University of Lethbridge Board of Governors Award
audience: Grade 12 students applying to University of Lethbridge — automatic consideration with admission application
description: The University of Lethbridge Board of Governors Award provides $1,000 to Grade 12 students pursuing post-secondary education. Students applying to the University of Lethbridge are automatically considered for this award based on their admission application, with no separate application process required.

title: University of Lethbridge Grade 11 Merit Award
audience: Grade 11 students planning to attend ULethbridge — 75% average and above
description: The University of Lethbridge awards this $800 merit scholarship to Grade 11 students who demonstrate strong academic performance and plan to attend ULethbridge for post-secondary studies. To qualify, students must maintain a 75% average or above.

title: LaDue Ladies Lunch Scholarship
audience: Female-identifying Grade 12 students in Alberta entering post-secondary
description: The LaDue Ladies Lunch Scholarship supports female-identifying Grade 12 students in Alberta who are entering post-secondary education. This $4,000 award recognizes and encourages young women pursuing their educational goals at the post-secondary level.

title: Bette Joan Rac Piano Scholarship
audience: Piano students in Alberta
description: This $1,000 scholarship supports piano students pursuing their musical education in Alberta. Offered to recognize excellence and passion in piano performance, it is open to high school students interested in continuing their musical studies.

title: Hec Gervais Academic and Curling Scholarship
audience: Alberta youth curlers eligible for U20 sanctioned season
description: This $3,000 scholarship recognizes Alberta youth curlers who demonstrate academic excellence and competitive curling participation. It is awarded to students eligible to compete in U20 sanctioned curling competitions during the academic year.

title: Lethbridge County Bursary Program
audience: First-year post-secondary students who are residents of Lethbridge County
notes: Three bursaries of $1,500 each. Financial need considered. Only for students entering first year of studies.
description: The Lethbridge County Bursary Program offers three awards of $1,500 each to support first-year post-secondary students from Lethbridge County. This bursary considers financial need as part of its selection process. Students must be residents of Lethbridge County and entering their first year of post-secondary studies to be eligible.

title: MindFuel Scholarship
audience: Alberta students entering first year of an undergraduate applied science or science education program
description: The MindFuel Scholarship supports Alberta students entering their first year of an undergraduate applied science or science education program. This $2,500 award recognizes students pursuing STEM fields and preparing for careers in science and technology. Eligible applicants must be graduating high school seniors preparing to enroll in a post-secondary institution.

title: High School Apprenticeship Scholarship
audience: Alberta high school students registered in the Registered Apprenticeship Program (RAP) or Career and Technology Studies (CTS) apprenticeship pathway
notes: No application required — consent to be considered in MyTradesecrets. Recipients notified by November 1.
description: This $1,000 scholarship is awarded to Alberta high school students enrolled in the Registered Apprenticeship Program (RAP) or Career and Technology Studies (CTS) apprenticeship pathway. Students are automatically considered for the award through MyTradesecrets with no application required, and recipients are notified by November 1st.

title: High School Apprenticeship Scholarship: Bright Futures
audience: Alberta high school students registered in both RAP and a CTS Apprenticeship Pathway
notes: No application required — consent to be considered in MyTradesecrets. Higher award for students completing both RAP and CTS pathway.
description: This $2,000 scholarship rewards Alberta high school students who are registered in both the Registered Apprenticeship Program (RAP) and a CTS Apprenticeship Pathway. No application is required—students are automatically considered through MyTradesecrets based on their enrollment. Students who successfully complete both the RAP and CTS pathway qualify for an enhanced award amount.

title: 4-H Canada Scholarships
audience: Active 4-H members in Alberta applying to post-secondary or trades programs
notes: Six different scholarship streams available. Must be a 4-H member in good standing.
description: 4-H Canada offers scholarships of $3,000 to active and in-good-standing 4-H members in Alberta who are pursuing post-secondary or trades education. Six different scholarship streams are available to support your continued learning. Applicants must demonstrate their commitment to 4-H and meet all membership requirements.

title: Dr. MacEwan Literary Arts Scholarship
audience: Alberta students 25 or younger demonstrating talent and clear goals in literary arts
notes: One scholarship awarded annually. Created in legacy of author and former Lieutenant Governor Dr. Grant MacEwan.
description: This annual $3,000 scholarship honours the legacy of Dr. Grant MacEwan, a renowned author and former Lieutenant Governor of Alberta. It recognizes Alberta high school students aged 25 or younger who demonstrate exceptional talent and clear aspirations in literary arts. One award is given each year to a deserving student pursuing their passion in writing and literature.

title: Alberta Foundation for the Arts Film and Video Arts Scholarship
audience: Alberta students 25 or younger demonstrating talent and goals in film and video arts
notes: One scholarship awarded annually by the Alberta Foundation for the Arts.
description: The Alberta Foundation for the Arts awards an annual $7,000 scholarship to Alberta students who demonstrate exceptional talent and commitment to film and video arts. Open to students aged 25 or younger, this award recognizes emerging artists pursuing goals in visual storytelling and multimedia creation.

title: Alberta Foundation for the Arts Performing Arts Scholarship
audience: Alberta students 25 or younger demonstrating talent and goals in performing arts
notes: One scholarship awarded annually by Alberta Culture.
description: Alberta Culture awards this $7,000 scholarship annually to recognize exceptional talent and dedication in the performing arts. It's open to Alberta students aged 25 or younger who are pursuing their passion in dance, theatre, music, and other performing disciplines. Applicants should demonstrate both artistic ability and clear goals in advancing their performing arts career.

title: Alberta Foundation for the Arts Visual Arts Scholarship
audience: Alberta students 25 or younger demonstrating talent and goals in visual arts
notes: One scholarship awarded annually by Alberta Culture.
description: Alberta Culture awards this $7,000 scholarship annually to recognize exceptional talent and achievement in visual arts. Open to Alberta students aged 25 or younger who demonstrate strong artistic ability and clear goals in visual arts studies or practice. One award is given each year to a deserving student showing promise in this creative field.

title: Enmax Environmental Scholarship
audience: Alberta students entering a diploma or degree program in Environmental Studies at a Canadian post-secondary institution
description: ENMAX offers this $1,000 scholarship to support Alberta students pursuing post-secondary education in Environmental Studies. Applicants must be graduating high school seniors planning to enter a diploma or degree program in Environmental Studies at a Canadian post-secondary institution.

title: Alberta Blue Cross Indigenous Scholarship
audience: Indigenous (First Nations, Métis, or Inuit) Alberta residents enrolled full-time in a post-secondary program of at least 2 years
notes: 9 scholarships awarded annually. Applications open October 5, 2026. Cannot have received this scholarship previously.
description: Alberta Blue Cross awards this $1,500 scholarship to Indigenous (First Nations, Métis, or Inuit) students who are enrolled full-time in post-secondary programs of at least 2 years in duration. Nine scholarships are awarded annually to recognize and support Indigenous learners pursuing their education. Applicants cannot have previously received this award.

title: Indspire Building Brighter Futures Bursaries and Scholarships
audience: First Nations, Inuit, and Métis students across Canada pursuing post-secondary education including trades and apprenticeships
notes: Canada's largest non-governmental funder of Indigenous post-secondary students. Multiple award streams available.
description: Indspire offers bursaries and scholarships for First Nations, Inuit, and Métis students pursuing post-secondary education across Canada, including trades and apprenticeships. As Canada's largest non-governmental funder of Indigenous post-secondary students, Indspire supports multiple award streams designed to help Indigenous students achieve their educational goals. Eligible students should connect with Indspire to learn more about specific award opportunities and application requirements.

title: Grant MacEwan United World College Scholarship
audience: High school students from across Alberta demonstrating exceptional potential in intellectual curiosity, leadership, and resilience
description: Grant MacEwan United World College offers this scholarship to high school students across Alberta who demonstrate exceptional potential in intellectual curiosity, leadership, and resilience. The award supports students who show promise in these key areas as they pursue post-secondary education.

title: Lois Hole Humanities and Social Sciences Scholarship
audience: Alberta students enrolled full-time in the Faculty of Humanities, Social Sciences, or Arts at an Alberta post-secondary institution
description: This $5,000 scholarship supports Alberta students pursuing full-time studies in Humanities, Social Sciences, or Arts at an Alberta post-secondary institution. The award recognizes academic excellence and commitment to these disciplines that build critical thinking and cultural understanding.

title: Louise McKinney Post-Secondary Scholarship
audience: Alberta students with outstanding academic achievement at a post-secondary institution in Alberta
description: The Louise McKinney Post-Secondary Scholarship recognizes Alberta students who demonstrate outstanding academic achievement while enrolled at a post-secondary institution within the province. This $2,500 award supports high-performing students pursuing their studies at Alberta's colleges and universities.

title: Mildred Rowe Weston Memorial Scholarship
audience: Alberta students who completed at least three courses through ADLC as shown on Alberta Transcript of High School Achievement
description: The Mildred Rowe Weston Memorial Scholarship awards $1,000 to Alberta high school students who have completed at least three courses through ADLC (Alberta Distance Learning Centre). This scholarship recognizes academic achievement among students utilizing distance learning education in Alberta.

title: Tiessen Foundation Broadcast Scholarship
audience: Alberta high school graduates enrolled full-time in a post-secondary program related to broadcasting
description: The Tiessen Foundation Broadcast Scholarship provides $750 to Alberta high school graduates pursuing full-time post-secondary studies in broadcasting. This award recognizes students committed to careers in the broadcast media field.

title: UCalgary President's Admission Scholarship
audience: First-year University of Calgary students with a 95%+ admission average
notes: No separate application required — awarded automatically upon admission with a 95%+ average. Any faculty, any citizenship.
description: The University of Calgary awards this $5,000 scholarship automatically to first-year students admitted with a 95% or higher average. No separate application is required—eligible students receive the award upon admission to any faculty at the University of Calgary.

title: MacEwan University Chancellor's Scholarship
audience: Canadian citizens or permanent residents entering a MacEwan degree program from high school with an 80%+ average
notes: No separate application — automatically considered upon admission. Amount scales with average: up to $14,000 (95–100%), $9,999 (90–95%), $5,999 (85–90%), $2,999 (80–85%). Renewable with GPA maintained.
description: MacEwan University awards this competitive scholarship to Canadian citizens and permanent residents entering a MacEwan degree program from high school with strong academic performance. The award is automatically considered upon admission and ranges from $2,999 to $14,000 depending on your admission average, with the potential to be renewed each year as long as you maintain your GPA.

title: Mount Royal University Entrance Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 students entering any MRU program with an 80%+ average
notes: Over $5.5 million awarded annually across all faculties. One application covers all MRU awards. Application window: November 1 – March 1.
description: Mount Royal University awards entrance scholarships to graduating high school students with strong academic achievement. Recipients must maintain an 80%+ average and be entering any MRU program. With over $5.5 million awarded annually across all faculties, this is a major opportunity for Alberta students seeking to pursue post-secondary education at MRU.

title: ATCO Indigenous Education High School Merit Award
audience: Self-identified First Nations, Inuit, or Métis students enrolled full-time in Grades 10–12 in Canada
notes: One of the few merit awards specifically for current high school students (Grades 10–12). Must reapply annually. Not open to children of ATCO employees.
description: ATCO offers this $750 merit award annually to self-identified First Nations, Inuit, or Métis high school students in Canada who demonstrate academic excellence. Open to students currently enrolled full-time in Grades 10–12, this award recognizes Indigenous student achievement and requires annual reapplication. Children of ATCO employees are not eligible.

title: TC Energy STEM & Trades Scholarships
audience: Students entering or enrolled in a STEM or trades program who reside near TC Energy operations in Canada
notes: 800+ scholarships available across Canada. STEM awards: $5,000; Trades awards: $2,500. Verify your community eligibility at TCScholarships.com. Not for dependants of TC Energy employees.
description: TC Energy offers $5,000 STEM scholarships and $2,500 trades scholarships to students entering or enrolled in post-secondary STEM or trades programs who reside near TC Energy operations in Canada. Over 800 scholarships are available nationwide. Applicants must verify their community eligibility and are not eligible if they are dependants of TC Energy employees.

title: RBC Ignite Scholarship
audience: Canadians ages 16–20 taking a job-ready skills course or certification in Canada
notes: Covers certifications and skills courses — lifeguarding, first aid, coding, language, graphic design, coach certification, and more. Open to current high school students. Closes when 500 applications are reached.
description: RBC Ignite offers $1,500 to support Canadians ages 16–20 pursuing job-ready skills and certifications. This award covers a wide range of practical courses including lifeguarding, first aid, coding, language training, graphic design, and coaching certification. Current high school students are eligible to apply.

title: MADD Canada Youth Bursary Fund
audience: Young Canadians severely injured or who lost an immediate family member in an impaired driving crash
notes: Top award (Louise Joanne Twerdy Award) is $10,000. Eligibility is specific to those personally affected by impaired driving. Must enrol full-time in an approved post-secondary program.
description: MADD Canada's Youth Bursary Fund supports young Canadians who have been personally affected by impaired driving—whether through serious injury or the loss of an immediate family member. This $10,000 award (top prize: Louise Joanne Twerdy Award) helps recipients pursue full-time studies at an approved post-secondary institution. Applicants must demonstrate their commitment to education while carrying the impact of an impaired driving tragedy.

title: Cenovus Energy Indigenous Scholarship
audience: Indigenous students (First Nations, Métis, Inuit) residing near Cenovus operating areas in Canada pursuing post-secondary education
notes: Administered through Indspire. Renewable up to 4 years ($5,000/year). Three intake windows annually: February 1, August 1, November 1. Cenovus operates extensively across Alberta.
description: Cenovus Energy, administered through Indspire, offers this $5,000 renewable scholarship to Indigenous students (First Nations, Métis, and Inuit) who reside near Cenovus operating areas in Canada and are pursuing post-secondary education. The award is renewable annually for up to four years and has three application intake windows each year.

title: Calgary Black Chambers Legacy Entrance Scholarship
audience: Black Canadian students graduating from a Calgary-region high school and entering first-year post-secondary
notes: Two awards of $2,500. Must graduate from a school in Airdrie, Calgary, Chestermere, Cochrane, High River, Okotoks, Springbank, Strathmore, or Diamond Valley. Minimum 70% GPA; financial need considered.
description: The Calgary Black Chambers Legacy Entrance Scholarship provides two awards of $2,500 each to Black Canadian students graduating from a high school in the Calgary region and entering their first year of post-secondary education. Applicants must have a minimum 70% GPA, and financial need will be considered as part of the selection process. Eligible schools include those located in Airdrie, Calgary, Chestermere, Cochrane, High River, Okotoks, Springbank, Strathmore, and Diamond Valley.

title: Skills Canada Alberta Terry Cooke Legacy Scholarship
audience: Top-scoring secondary school student representing Alberta at the Skills Canada National Competition
notes: No application required — automatically awarded to the highest-scoring Alberta secondary student at Skills Canada Nationals. Worth $5,000/year for up to 4 years ($20,000 total). Separate from the WorldSkills Provincial Champion Scholarship.
description: Skills Canada Alberta automatically awards this $20,000 scholarship to the highest-scoring Alberta secondary school student competing at the Skills Canada National Competition. The award is worth $5,000 per year for up to four years and recognizes outstanding achievement in trades and technical skills. No application is required—winners are selected based on their competition performance.

title: Canada's Luckiest Student
audience: All students in Canada
notes: Annual giveaway — no essay or grades required. Prize bundle includes rent for a year, $2,000 in groceries, a trip for two to the Galapagos, and a $20,000 cheque. Enter for free in ~2 minutes. Earlier entries earn more entries in the draw.
description: Canada's Luckiest Student is an annual giveaway open to all students in Canada, with no essay or grades required to enter. The prize bundle includes a year of rent, $2,000 in groceries, a trip for two to the Galapagos, and a $20,000 cheque. Entries are free and take about 2 minutes to complete, with earlier submissions receiving more chances to win.

title: Wolf Scholars Program
audience: Canadian citizens or permanent residents entering U of T Faculty of Arts & Science (St. George) with 90–100% average
notes: Up to 16 scholars selected per year. Fully funded: tuition, fees, living stipend, travel, internships, mentorship, and seminars. Open to 400+ Arts & Science programs (excluding Commerce). Applications open September 11, 2026.
description: The Wolf Scholars Program is a fully funded national scholarship for outstanding students entering the University of Toronto's Faculty of Arts & Science (St. George campus). Selected scholars receive comprehensive support including tuition, fees, living stipend, travel, internships, mentorship, and seminars. Up to 16 scholars are selected annually from Canadian citizens and permanent residents with a 90–100% average across 400+ Arts & Science programs (excluding Commerce).

targetInstitutions: University of Toronto Faculty of Arts & Science (St. George)

title: Electronic Recycling Association Scholarship
audience: Full-time or part-time students in Canada
notes: Competition-based: create a marketing plan and organize an e-waste collection event in your area. Up to 12 winners of $10,000 each, plus a MacBook Pro. Students outside ERA's main cities (Vancouver, Calgary, Edmonton, Saskatoon, Winnipeg, Toronto, Halifax, Montreal) have adjusted requirements.
description: The Electronic Recycling Association offers a $10,000 scholarship and MacBook Pro to full-time or part-time students in Canada who demonstrate initiative in environmental sustainability. Winners are selected through a competition requiring applicants to create a marketing plan and organize an e-waste collection event in their area, with up to 12 awards available. Students in major Canadian cities have standard requirements, while those outside ERA's main cities (Vancouver, Calgary, Edmonton, Saskatoon, Winnipeg, Toronto, Halifax, Montreal) may have adjusted participation requirements.

title: Alberta Masonic Higher Education Bursary
audience: Alberta and NWT residents with financial need entering post-secondary
notes: 30 bursaries of $6,000 awarded annually. Based on financial need and scholastic ability. First-year students given priority. Deadline is Feb 1 at noon.
description: The Alberta Masonic Higher Education Bursary is awarded by the Alberta Masonic Foundation to support first-year students entering post-secondary education. Worth $6,000, this bursary recognizes both scholastic ability and demonstrated financial need, with 30 awards distributed annually to Alberta and NWT residents.

title: Alberta Junior Athletic Award
audience: Alberta residents competing on a designated provincial junior sport team and entering post-secondary
notes: Designated junior sports include ACAC and AUAA sanctioned teams. Minimum 2.0 GPA required. Apply via Alberta Student Aid.
description: This $800 award recognizes Alberta residents who compete on designated provincial junior sports teams (ACAC and AUAA sanctioned) and are entering post-secondary studies. To qualify, applicants must maintain a minimum 2.0 GPA and apply through Alberta Student Aid.

title: Alberta Golf Association Foundation Scholarships
audience: Alberta golfers entering post-secondary
notes: 50+ awards annually totalling roughly $50,000. Criteria include academic performance, financial need, volunteer involvement, and golf participation.
description: The Alberta Golf Association Foundation offers over 50 scholarships annually totalling approximately $50,000 to support Alberta golfers pursuing post-secondary education. Awards recognize strong academic performance, demonstrated financial need, volunteer contributions, and active participation in golf. This is an excellent opportunity for talented golfers to offset education costs while pursuing their goals.

title: Football Alberta Scholarships
audience: Graduating Grade 12 ASAA tackle football players continuing to play at the post-secondary level in Alberta
notes: 8 scholarships of $2,000 each. Recipients must be registered full-time at an accredited Alberta post-secondary institution and actively participating on a university or junior football team.
description: Football Alberta offers eight $2,000 scholarships annually to graduating Grade 12 tackle football players who are continuing their athletic career at the post-secondary level. Recipients must be registered full-time at an accredited Alberta post-secondary institution and actively playing on a university or junior football team. This award recognizes student-athletes who have demonstrated excellence in high school football and are committed to advancing their sport in Alberta.

title: ASAA Pay It Forward Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 Alberta student-athletes who coached or officiated at the school or community level
notes: One award per ASAA zone (8 zones total). Must have participated in at least one ASAA-sanctioned sport and coached or officiated during high school. Contact your school's career centre.
description: The ASAA Pay It Forward Scholarship recognizes Grade 12 Alberta student-athletes who have given back to their school and community by coaching or officiating sports. With one award of $500 available per ASAA zone, this scholarship celebrates students who have participated in ASAA-sanctioned sports while contributing to others' athletic development.

title: Queen's Platinum Jubilee Scholarship for Performing Arts
audience: Alberta students with exceptional talent in performing arts — rotating annually between music, theatre, and dance
notes: One scholarship per year. 2026 cycle was dance; 2027 cycle is music. School nomination required. Contact your guidance counsellor early — internal deadlines precede the provincial one.
description: The Queen's Platinum Jubilee Scholarship for Performing Arts awards $7,000 annually to Alberta high school students demonstrating exceptional talent in performing arts. The award rotates yearly among music, theatre, and dance disciplines, requiring school nomination and guidance counsellor involvement. Eligible students should contact their guidance counsellor early, as internal school deadlines precede the provincial application deadline.

title: Alberta Centennial Award
audience: Alberta high school graduates nominated for the Premier's Citizenship Award who are enrolling in post-secondary
notes: 25 awards of $2,005 each. Eligibility flows from the Premier's Citizenship Award nomination — only nominated students can apply. Contact your school administration.
description: The Alberta Centennial Award provides $2,005 to Alberta high school graduates who have been nominated for the Premier's Citizenship Award and are enrolling in post-secondary education. This award recognizes exceptional citizenship and community contribution among graduating high school students across the province. Eligible students must be nominated through the Premier's Citizenship Award program; applicants should contact their school administration for nomination details.

title: Aufricht Family Fund Student Award
audience: Graduating Calgary CBE or CCSD students entering UCalgary or SAIT with financial need
notes: Renewable for 3 years with a 2.0+ cumulative GPA and full-time enrollment. Financial need required. Cannot already hold an equal or greater award from EducationMatters or Calgary Foundation.
description: The Aufricht Family Fund provides $4,000–$5,000 awards to graduating Calgary high school students entering post-secondary studies with demonstrated financial need. This renewable award supports students for up to 3 years if they maintain a 2.0+ cumulative GPA and remain enrolled full-time. Applicants from Calgary CBE or CCSD schools who plan to attend UCalgary or SAIT are encouraged to apply, provided they do not already hold an equal or greater award from EducationMatters or the Calgary Foundation.

title: Elmer and Ona Hansen Memorial Fund
audience: Alberta rural farm youth entering first-year post-secondary with no prior post-secondary enrollment
notes: Multiple large awards: 1 × $20,000, 1 × $15,000, 1 × $10,000, 7 × $5,000. Applicants must be Alberta rural farm young persons who have not previously started or completed any post-secondary program. Applications open in May.
description: The Elmer and Ona Hansen Memorial Fund provides substantial scholarships for Alberta rural farm youth pursuing their first year of post-secondary education. With awards ranging from $5,000 to $20,000, this program supports students from farming backgrounds who are beginning their post-secondary journey. Applicants must be from rural Alberta farms and have no prior post-secondary education.

title: AAAF Memorial Bursary
audience: Alberta residents entering an agriculture or environmental science program at a college or university
notes: Offered by the Association of Alberta Agricultural Fieldmen. Must submit high school marks and a letter of acceptance from a post-secondary institution. Apply through your local County agricultural office.
description: The Association of Alberta Agricultural Fieldmen offers this $1,000 bursary to Alberta residents entering agriculture or environmental science programs at post-secondary institutions. Applicants must submit high school marks and a letter of acceptance from their chosen college or university. Apply through your local County agricultural office.

title: AHSRA Scholarships
audience: Grade 12 Alberta High School Rodeo Association members and event volunteers
notes: One application covers all AHSRA awards: Merit Awards, NHSRA Merit Awards, Canadian Finals Scholarships, Presidents Award, Teskey Top Hand Award, and Raffle Scholarship. Submit by mail to the AHSRA Scholarship Coordinator.
description: The Alberta High School Rodeo Association (AHSRA) offers multiple scholarships for Grade 12 students who are active members or volunteers in the association. These awards—including Merit Awards, NHSRA Merit Awards, Canadian Finals Scholarships, Presidents Award, Teskey Top Hand Award, and Raffle Scholarship—recognize both athletic achievement and community involvement. A single application covers all available AHSRA scholarships.

title: Roane Family Bursary for Queen's University
audience: Students from Canmore, Banff, or Morley attending Queen's University
notes: Based on residency in Canmore, Banff, or Morley and demonstrated financial need. $5,000 per year. Contact your school guidance counsellor for application details.
description: The Roane Family Bursary supports students from Canmore, Banff, or Morley who are attending Queen's University. This $5,000 annual bursary is awarded based on demonstrated financial need. Applicants should contact their school guidance counsellor for application details.

title: Volleyball Alberta Hugh Hoyles Scholarship Fund
audience: Alberta residents selected to a Team Alberta volleyball program
notes: Must be an Alberta resident selected to a Team Alberta Program. Only one application accepted per calendar year.
description: Volleyball Alberta offers the Hugh Hoyles Scholarship Fund to support student-athletes excelling in volleyball. This $500 award recognizes Alberta residents who have been selected to a Team Alberta volleyball program. Applicants may submit only one application per calendar year.

title: PEO Florence E. Taylor Charitable Scholarship Fund
audience: Female Alberta students in their first or second year at an Alberta or Saskatchewan post-secondary institution
notes: Offered by the P.E.O. Sisterhood. Contact your nearest Alberta P.E.O. chapter to apply. First and second year students preferred. Financial need considered.
description: The P.E.O. Sisterhood offers the Florence E. Taylor Charitable Scholarship Fund to support female Alberta students pursuing post-secondary education. This award is available to first- and second-year students attending institutions in Alberta or Saskatchewan, with financial need considered in the selection process. Interested applicants should contact their nearest Alberta P.E.O. chapter for application details.

title: University of Alberta Turtle Spirit Pathway Award
audience: Domestic students applying to a UAlberta direct-entry undergraduate program with no prior post-secondary and demonstrated financial barriers
notes: Up to 30 new students per year. Must have no prior post-secondary coursework. Separate application required via Awards Hub after applying for UAlberta admission.
description: The University of Alberta offers the Turtle Spirit Pathway Award to support domestic students with demonstrated financial barriers who are entering a UAlberta direct-entry undergraduate program with no prior post-secondary experience. Up to 30 new students are selected each year, and applicants must complete a separate application through the Awards Hub after submitting their UAlberta admission application.

title: Beyond the North Scholarship
audience: Grade 12 students graduating from a Fairview area high school in northern Alberta and entering first-year post-secondary
notes: Established in 2021 by alumni from the Fairview, Alberta area. Open to any Canadian post-secondary institution. Administered through Calgary Foundation.
description: The Beyond the North Scholarship, established in 2021 by Fairview area alumni and administered through the Calgary Foundation, supports Grade 12 graduates from Fairview area high schools in northern Alberta as they pursue first-year post-secondary studies. This award is open to Canadian students entering any Canadian post-secondary institution.

title: Charmaine Letourneau Scholarship
audience: Alberta residents who are deaf or hard of hearing entering a post-secondary or vocational program
notes: Must demonstrate financial need and knowledge of sign language. School and community leadership considered. Apply through the Edmonton Community Foundation.
description: The Edmonton Community Foundation awards the Charmaine Letourneau Scholarship to Alberta residents who are deaf or hard of hearing as they enter a post-secondary or vocational program. Applicants must demonstrate financial need and knowledge of sign language, with school and community leadership also considered in selection.

title: Royal Canadian Legion Ladies Auxiliary AB-NWT Bursary
audience: Alberta and NWT students entering first-term post-secondary with a family connection to veterans, RCMP, firefighters, or Legion members
notes: Must be a graduate of the current or previous year and under 21. Eligible family connections include children/grandchildren of veterans, current Canadian Forces, RCMP, reserve personnel, paid or volunteer firefighters, and Legion Auxiliary or Branch members. Contact your nearest Alberta Legion branch for an application.
description: The Royal Canadian Legion Ladies Auxiliary in Alberta and the Northwest Territories offers this $500 bursary to graduating high school students entering their first year of post-secondary education. To qualify, applicants must have a family connection to veterans, current Canadian Forces members, RCMP officers, reserve personnel, firefighters (paid or volunteer), or Legion Auxiliary or Branch members. Recipients must be under 21 years old and can contact their nearest Alberta Legion branch to apply.

title: UFCW Canada Begg's-Dowling-Mathieu Scholarship
audience: UFCW Canada members or their dependents/spouses entering full-time post-secondary studies in Canada
notes: 18 scholarships of $1,000 allocated nationally by region. Does not require top grades — enrollment and passion for learning are the main criteria. Apply online at ufcw.ca. Parent or guardian must be an active UFCW Canada member in good standing.
description: UFCW Canada offers this $1,000 scholarship to members in good standing or their dependents and spouses who are entering full-time post-secondary studies in Canada. The scholarship recognizes enrollment and passion for learning rather than top grades. Applicants must have a parent or guardian who is an active UFCW Canada member to be eligible.

title: UFCW Local 401 Scholarships
audience: UFCW Local 401 (Alberta) members or their dependents entering post-secondary
notes: Two separate scholarships: the Robert McWilliams Memorial Scholarship and the Grant Notley Memorial Scholarship. Parent or guardian must be a UFCW Local 401 member. Up to $2,500 available. Apply through gounion.ca.
description: UFCW Local 401 offers two separate scholarships—the Robert McWilliams Memorial Scholarship and the Grant Notley Memorial Scholarship—worth up to $2,500 to support members' dependents as they enter post-secondary education. To be eligible, your parent or guardian must be a UFCW Local 401 member in Alberta. Applications are submitted through gounion.ca.

title: Scotiabank x myBlueprint Scholarships
audience: Grade 12 students across Canada with a myBlueprint account
notes: Four scholarship streams: Diversity, Financial Wellness, Future Women Leaders, and STEM. One winner per stream guaranteed per region (Alberta is grouped with MB, SK, NT, NU). 16 winners nationally at $3,750 each. Two-phase process: short application, then video submission for finalists. Access via your school's myBlueprint account.
description: Scotiabank offers four scholarship streams—Diversity, Financial Wellness, Future Women Leaders, and STEM—through myBlueprint for Grade 12 students across Canada. One winner per stream is guaranteed per region (Alberta grouped with MB, SK, NT, NU), with 16 national winners at $3,750 each. Eligible students apply through a two-phase process: an initial short application followed by a video submission for selected finalists, accessed via their school's myBlueprint account.

title: Red Deer Polytechnic High School Entrance Scholarship
audience: Current high school students with an 80%+ average in five 5-credit grade 11 or 12 subjects planning to attend RDP
notes: Email your transcript or detailed academic report to the RDP Student Connect Centre along with an up-to-date email address and phone number. Limited awards — apply early. Applies to any credit program at Red Deer Polytechnic.
description: Red Deer Polytechnic offers this $1,000 scholarship to high school students with an 80%+ average in five 5-credit grade 11 or 12 subjects who are planning to attend RDP. The award applies to any credit program at Red Deer Polytechnic and recognizes strong academic achievement among incoming students.

title: Red Deer Polytechnic Regional Access & Excellence Scholarship
audience: Students entering RDP full-time who graduated from a listed Central Alberta high school in the most recent year
notes: Automatically considered based on completed General Application. Eligible schools include Lindsay Thurber, Hunting Hills, Notre Dame, Lacombe Composite, Innisfail, Drumheller Valley, Olds, Stettler, Rocky Mountain House, and many others. See RDP's full school list.
description: Red Deer Polytechnic (RDP) offers this $1,000 scholarship to recognize academic excellence among students entering full-time studies at the institution. Eligible students must have graduated from a qualifying Central Alberta high school in the most recent year and are automatically considered upon completing RDP's General Application.

title: A. Bernard & Mary B. Dixon Memorial Scholarship
audience: Students from the Red Deer and Central Alberta area entering post-secondary
notes: Administered by the Community Foundation of Central Alberta (CFCAB). Funds are disbursed directly to the post-secondary institution. Two signed reference letters required. Application available at cfcab.ca.
description: The Community Foundation of Central Alberta (CFCAB) administers this academic scholarship for students from the Red Deer and Central Alberta area. Applicants must be graduating high school seniors entering a post-secondary institution, and the award funds are sent directly to the school. Two signed reference letters are required as part of the application process.

title: Red Deer Regional Health Foundation Scholarship
audience: Central Alberta residents pursuing post-secondary education in a healthcare field
notes: Offered by the Red Deer Regional Health Foundation for residents of Central Alberta entering any level of healthcare training. Successful applicants notified by email in May. Apply at rdrhfoundation.com.
description: The Red Deer Regional Health Foundation offers this scholarship to residents of Central Alberta who are pursuing post-secondary education in a healthcare field. The award supports students entering any level of healthcare training at post-secondary institutions. Successful applicants are notified by email in May.

title: Alberta Moose Association Youth Awareness Scholarship
audience: Alberta grade 9–12 students who participated in the AMA Youth Awareness KidsTalks program
notes: Students who complete a minimum of three KidsTalks presentations at an Association Student Congress are eligible. Top presenters at the International Student Congress win $2,000–$12,000. Local entries earn $1,000 for entering an Alberta college or university. Contact your nearest Moose Lodge to participate.
description: The Alberta Moose Association offers this scholarship to recognize youth who participate in their KidsTalks awareness program. Grade 9–12 students who complete at least three presentations at an Association Student Congress are eligible to win $1,000–$12,000, with top presenters at the International Student Congress earning up to $12,000.

title: Kin Canada Bursary
audience: Canadian students entering post-secondary with demonstrated community and school involvement
notes: Offered by Kin Canada (formerly Kinsmen/Kinette clubs). Based on community involvement, school participation, and leadership. Apply through your local Kin Club or via kincanada.ca. Separate from the Kinsmen Club of Medicine Hat grant already in the database.
description: Kin Canada (formerly Kinsmen/Kinette clubs) offers this $1,000 bursary to Canadian students entering post-secondary who have demonstrated strong community and school involvement. The award recognizes leadership, community service, and active participation in school activities. Applicants can apply through their local Kin Club or via kincanada.ca.

title: Mensa Canada Scholarship Programme
audience: Canadian students enrolled full-time at a Canadian post-secondary institution
notes: Not restricted to Mensa members. Selection is entirely essay-based. No GPA requirement. Essay topic changes annually. Apply at canada.mensa.org. Multiple awards ranging from $1,000 to $2,500.
description: Mensa Canada awards multiple scholarships ranging from $1,000 to $2,500 to Canadian students enrolled full-time at Canadian post-secondary institutions. Selection is based entirely on an essay submission; there is no GPA requirement, and the scholarship is open to all students regardless of Mensa membership. Applicants can learn more and apply at canada.mensa.org.

title: Rogers Birdies for Kids / AltaLink Scholarship
audience: Graduating Grade 12 students entering first-year post-secondary with involvement in a Rogers Birdies for Kids presented by AltaLink participating charity
notes: Must demonstrate community involvement through a Birdies for Kids participating charity and provide a reference letter from a charity representative. Minimum 70% GPA. Administered by Calgary Foundation.
description: The Calgary Foundation offers this scholarship to recognize graduating Grade 12 students who demonstrate meaningful community involvement through a Rogers Birdies for Kids presented by AltaLink participating charity. Applicants must maintain a minimum 70% GPA and provide a reference letter from a charity representative. This award supports students entering their first year of post-secondary education.

title: Harvey Northcott Memorial Scholarship
audience: Alberta students with a connection to agriculture, rodeo, or the Leduc community
notes: Two scholarships of $1,000 each. Funded by the Leduc Black Gold Rodeo & Exhibition Association in memory of Harvey Northcott. Apply at blackgoldrodeo.com. 2026 deadline has passed — note for next cycle.
description: The Leduc Black Gold Rodeo & Exhibition Association offers two $1,000 scholarships annually in memory of Harvey Northcott, supporting Alberta high school students with a connection to agriculture, rodeo, or the Leduc community. This award recognizes students who embody the spirit of ranching, agricultural pursuits, or community involvement in the rodeo tradition.

title: Rotary Career Opportunity Award
audience: Graduating students from Red Deer Public or Catholic school divisions with financial need, planning to attend an Alberta post-secondary institution
notes: Up to 15 awards annually. Applications available from school counsellors in February. Submit online via grantinterface.ca by 4:30 pm on the deadline date.
