description: The Rotary Career Opportunity Award is offered by Rotary to support graduating high school students from the Red Deer area who demonstrate financial need and plan to pursue post-secondary education in Alberta. Up to 15 awards of $3,000 are available annually to eligible students from Red Deer Public or Catholic school divisions.

title: William Arthur Bower Memorial Scholarship
audience: Graduating students from Red Deer Public or Catholic school divisions
notes: Minimum 5 awards annually; renewable for up to 4 years. In memory of a Red Deer High School graduate who died in WWI. Contact your school guidance counsellor.
description: The William Arthur Bower Memorial Scholarship honours the legacy of a Red Deer High School graduate who died in World War I. This $5,000 award recognizes academic achievement among graduating students from Red Deer Public or Catholic school divisions. With a minimum of 5 awards given annually and renewable for up to 4 years, this scholarship supports students as they transition to post-secondary education.

title: Red Deer Arts Council Canada Centennial Secondary Scholarship
audience: High school students (grades 9–12) in Red Deer or Central Alberta pursuing arts
notes: Must reside in or have immediate family as principal residents in Red Deer or Central Alberta (roughly Ponoka to Olds, Rocky Mountain House to Stettler). Arts submission required.
description: The Red Deer Arts Council awards this $1,000 scholarship to high school students in Red Deer and Central Alberta who are pursuing the arts. Applicants must reside in or have immediate family as principal residents in the region (roughly Ponoka to Olds, Rocky Mountain House to Stettler) and must submit an arts portfolio or application demonstrating their commitment to the arts.

title: Red Deer Arts Council Waskasoo Bluegrass Music Scholarship
audience: Secondary music students in Red Deer or Central Alberta continuing music at post-secondary
notes: For students continuing music education at post-secondary level. Must reside in Red Deer or Central Alberta.
description: The Red Deer Arts Council offers this $1,000 scholarship to support secondary music students in Red Deer and Central Alberta who are continuing their music education at the post-secondary level. This award recognizes students' commitment to pursuing music in higher education and values the importance of arts in our community.

title: Trey Purdie Memorial Scholarship
audience: Graduating students from Red Deer County or Chinook's Edge School Division living on a working farm or ranch, or Alberta High School Rodeo Association members
notes: Two streams: (1) CESD/Red Deer County students on a working farm/ranch — deadline May 31; (2) AHSRA members in good standing — deadline April 1. Amounts differ by stream.
description: The Trey Purdie Memorial Scholarship supports graduating high school students from Red Deer County and Chinook's Edge School Division who are actively involved in agriculture. The scholarship has two streams: one for students living and working on a farm or ranch, and another for members in good standing with the Alberta High School Rodeo Association.

title: University of Lethbridge Chinook Scholarship
audience: Graduating high school students entering the University of Lethbridge with a minimum 85% average and demonstrated leadership
notes: Reference letter required. Must enroll full-time in both Fall and Spring semesters immediately following the award.
description: The University of Lethbridge offers the Chinook Scholarship to support graduating high school students who demonstrate academic excellence and strong leadership qualities. This $5,000 award is for students entering the University of Lethbridge full-time and maintaining enrollment through both fall and spring semesters. Applicants must have a minimum 85% average and provide a reference letter.

title: University of Lethbridge High School Entrance Awards
audience: Graduating high school students entering the University of Lethbridge
notes: Pool of named entrance awards. Criteria vary by award — some consider academic average, others leadership, financial need, or artistic ability. Apply via the Bridge student portal.
description: The University of Lethbridge offers entrance awards of up to $6,000 for graduating high school students entering the university. These awards are available through a pool of named entrance scholarships with varying criteria—some consider academic average, others focus on leadership, financial need, or artistic ability. Students apply through the Bridge student portal.

title: Lethbridge Polytechnic Entrance Award
audience: Students admitted to Lethbridge Polytechnic full-time
notes: One application covers 400+ awards worth over $800,000 total. Application opens March 1; notifications in early August. Alberta residents may also access Jason Lang and Louise McKinney provincial scholarships through the same application.
description: Lethbridge Polytechnic offers entrance awards to students admitted to full-time programs at the institution. With over 400 awards worth $800,000+ available through a single application, this is a major scholarship opportunity for qualifying students. Alberta residents can also apply for provincial scholarships (Jason Lang and Louise McKinney) using the same application.
